_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of: 2026-08-25 (evening) · A second long live session. Sam edited the GR Priorities register in a browser and hit a save that failed with a message blaming his sign-in — it was not his account. Refresh tokens are replaced each time they are used, and a browser tab still holding the previous one overwrote the good copy with the spent one, which signed him out of every tab at once. Fixed so the newest credential always wins. He then supplied three authenticated PDFs of brand-new law: SB 135 created an Education Code article for Credit for Prior Learning, effective 13 July. Reading all sixteen register entries against it found that one of them — ranked second — is asking the Legislature for something it has already passed. The register also could not cite the new law at all, because its citation rules never covered that range of section numbers. Sam then named what he wants built: that whole-register pass, as a button, able to propose entirely new priorities. It is built. Sierra also ran out of API credit this evening and was returning errors to the public; Sam restored it the same evening, and the uptime monitor did raise the alert correctly.
_status: Everything from this session is merged and live, and the Sierra outage is resolved — Sam restored the credit balance the same evening. Two decisions in the register are legal judgments waiting on him: whether entry #2 is rewritten now that reciprocity is law, and whether entry #12 answers an objection the new statute hands to a reader. Nothing was written to the register; every finding is a proposal.

items.text: Sierra ran out of API credit this evening and you restored it — thank you. That is the third time (21 Aug, 22 Aug, 25 Aug). The uptime monitor did its job and raised the alert, but it only looks every three hours, so an outage can run that long before anyone is told. A balance-threshold alert on the Anthropic account itself would catch it before it becomes an outage, and that is the one thing a monitor here cannot do.

Sierra is running on Haiku 4.5 as the temporary cost measure you asked for — about a third the price of what it was on (Sonnet, not Opus). When corporate billing is released, switching back needs no code change and no session: set CPL_CHAT_MODEL on the Supabase project to claude-sonnet-4-6. Worth trying the whole-register sweep on Haiku once before you rely on it — a sixteen-row legal analysis is the hardest thing the assistant does, and it is where a smaller model would show first.

Settled, and noted so nobody undoes it: the automated check found 40 of 41 answers still correct on Haiku, and the one it dropped was the caveat beside the big waiting-credit number — the reminder that roughly a third of reviewed credit is correctly ruled Not Applicable, so the total is a ceiling rather than a debt. You said you can live with it for now, so it stays as it is. The fix is written down and ready if you change your mind: move that caveat next to the number itself instead of into a rules list further away, which would make it stick on any model.

Entry #2 (reciprocity between colleges) now asks for something already law. The new Education Code §78093.2(b)(2) requires every campus to accept transcribed prior-learning credit from other campuses. The entry still asks for a trailer bill, and it is ranked second, so it is near the top of what the Chancellor's Office reads. Two things do survive: 'no secondary review' is not stated outright, and the CSU/UC half is weaker in the statute than in the trailer bill.

Entry #12 is the one we call the cleanest win, and the new statute hands a reader an objection to it — §78093.1(f)(2) requires prior learning be 'approved through established curricular processes'. The answer exists (that governs how mastery is assessed, not what a course outline must list), but the entry is written as though nothing could be said against it. Worth pre-empting rather than meeting in the room.

The new law imposes four duties no entry covers. The biggest: every campus must evaluate the prior learning of ALL incoming students at the point their education plan is completed. Press 'Sweep this area' and the routine proposes these as new entries — nothing is added until you press Add, and anything added arrives marked 'proposed' with its citations flagged as machine-extracted.

None of the twenty register entries has had its citations checked against a primary source. The three PDFs you supplied are stamped 'authenticated electronic legal material', so they are the first material in the register that can move that number off zero.

Two things only a browser can confirm: that signing in and saving now works across several open tabs at once, and that 'Sweep this area' reads usefully. Sixteen verdicts is a lot on one screen — entries needing rework are listed first deliberately, but the density is your call.

The Common Course Reference map is the landing view, but the work surface behind it exists for only 5 of 159 subjects — so a curator clicking into it lands on nothing most of the time. Build the per-discipline decision packs, fetched on demand. The sharding path already exists.

The project memory's My College entry has grown into an append-only log — it is flagged by the documentation lint and has been carried across three sessions now. Compact it: current truth stays, the history moves to that workstream's lessons file.
